channel.title: The taxmetter blog
channel.description: Plain-English guides to 1099 taxes, deductions and quarterly payments for freelancers and contractors.

item.title: How much should I set aside for taxes on 1099 income?
item.description: Setting aside 20–30% is a good start, but your real number depends on your income, expenses and filing status. Here’s how to work it out.

item.title: Self-employment tax explained: what the 15.3% really pays for
item.description: Self-employment tax is often the biggest tax a new freelancer pays. Here’s what it is, how it’s worked out, and the legal ways to lower it.

item.title: Quarterly estimated taxes for 2026: due dates and how much to pay
item.description: If you expect to owe $1,000 or more, the IRS wants tax four times a year, not once in April. Here are the 2026 dates and the rules that keep you penalty-free.

item.title: 9 tax deductions freelancers often miss
item.description: Every legitimate business expense lowers both your income tax and your self-employment tax. These are the ones that most often get left off.

item.title: Home office deduction: simplified or regular method?
item.description: There are two ways to claim a home office. One takes five minutes, the other can be worth more. Here’s how to choose.

item.title: New 1099 thresholds for 2026: what changed and what didn’t
item.description: Clients now send a 1099-NEC at $2,000 instead of $600, and the 1099-K is back to $20,000. But one thing hasn’t changed: all your income is still taxable.
